drafter.rationale_plain: Photos show a consistent single-story ranch matching house number 6052 (b350807c) throughout the session. Clear before-to-after change is documented: tall grass measured with a ruler in Before shots (bc84960c, c4cb247f) versus grass trimmed to under 2 inches in After (febc36b2), with mowed front, side, and rear lawns visible in the genuine After batch (ff6d8d5a, 174960b0, 58809f4d, cadc5ef2, a965cde3). However, one photo (da6901e4) shows an unrelated address and out-of-sequence timestamp, and three photos labeled "After" (7b408915, 2ccee272, e1f7191a) were taken only seconds after Before/Condition shots, before mowing began — 2ccee272 still shows uncut weeds under an "After" label. Genuine completion evidence exists elsewhere in the set despite this documentation reshuffling.

verifier.rationale_plain: The order property, 6052, is confirmed by the visible house number in photo b350807c. GPS-inlier After photos (ff6d8d5a, cadc5ef2, 58809f4d, 174960b0, ef3981ad, 10ec2051) show the front, rear, sides and under-deck mowed with visible mow lines, and during photos show mowing and edging — real work at the verified property. However, nearly half the photos are GPS outliers about 102 km away, mostly overgrown Before shots, and da6901e4 shows a different address ('1801') far away. Two outlier After photos (2ccee272, e1f7191a) show uncut weeds and a different yard. The audit also flags tree branches over the shed (87c9a871) and a torn window screen (24991715). These conflicting records need a human check before release.
verifier.notes_for_human: Verified 6052 lawn was cut to standard in the GPS-inlier After photos, so completion evidence is genuine. But documentation is contaminated: a wrong-address photo (da6901e4 '1801', ~173 km) and a large cluster of ~102 km GPS outliers (overgrown Before shots), plus two outlier After photos showing uncut weeds/a different yard, suggest before/after mixing across properties. Please confirm these are stray/misfiled photos rather than photo-farming before paying, and route the audit-flagged tree overhang and torn window screen to condition reporting.
